One business stands out at Home Depot (HD): SRS, an acquisition that now sells through Home Depot's stores and that bulls may be betting on. You probably see Home Depot as a store chain tied to housing. Management says housing turnover has been low for four years, and Home Depot stock lost 16.9% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained 16.5%. That is the contradiction: a business that may be growing faster than the rest of Home Depot sits inside a stock that has trailed the market. So is SRS really growing faster than the rest of Home Depot?

SRS Is Outgrowing The Rest Of Home Depot

So far, yes. During the quarter that ended August 2, 2026, SRS grew its comparable sales faster than Home Depot as a whole. Overall comparable sales for the company rose 1.7%. SRS was positive in all of its verticals, and management said on the August 18, 2026 call that it looks to be taking significant share.

Management expects SRS to keep growing for the year. It guided the business to mid-single-digit organic sales growth for fiscal 2026. For the whole company, management guided a different measure, comparable sales growth of flat to 2%.

One number shows how far SRS has spread: 90%. That is the share of Home Depot's stores that closed a sale through SRS within the last 12 months, management said, so SRS no longer sits apart from the stores.

Home Depot's Margin Has Slipped For Three Years

Home Depot's profit has not kept up with SRS's growth so far. Its operating margin was 14.9% over the twelve months that ended July 30, 2023. The figure slipped to 13.9% a year later. Operating margin fell again to 13.1% in the twelve months to August 3, 2025 and to 12.4% in the twelve months to August 2, 2026. That marks the lowest rate at any of the past 40 quarter ends.

The latest quarter's gross margin looked better, and that is where the worry sits. On the same call, the question came up whether Home Depot would have missed profit forecasts without a tariff refund. Management said the company would have beaten its own expectations regardless. By management's count, the refund added about 145 basis points to gross margin, yet gross margin rose only about 25 basis points from a year earlier. About 60 basis points of it went to higher fuel, energy and input costs, and about 60 more went to the mix of the GMS and Mingledorff's acquisitions.

Home Depot does get more sales from those acquisitions. Management expects total sales to grow about 2.5% to 4.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the GMS acquisition, new stores, new branches and tuck-in acquisitions. But management also expects the unplanned input costs to fully offset the tariff refunds over the year.

Target (TGT) stock rose 73.2% over the past year. That marks the biggest gain in a group of six retailers that includes Walmart and Costco. Yet Target still costs less against its earnings than any of those rivals. The price appears to assume Target's sales will keep trailing most of its rivals and its margin, helped by tariff refunds, will not hold. So how much less are you paying, and what do you get for it?

What You Get For Target's Lower Price

You pay far less. Target trades at 15.8 times its earnings over its past four quarters, against 42.4 times for Walmart in the same retail industry.

For that lower price, you get a business that keeps more of each sales dollar as operating profit. Target posts 5.6%, compared with 4.4% for Walmart. In return, you give up growth: Target's sales rose 2.0% over its past four quarters, while Walmart's rose 6.2%.

Amazon, Costco and Home Depot also trade at a higher P/E than Target and grow sales faster. Target's margin sits above Costco's, but Amazon and Home Depot earn higher margins at 12.1% and 12.4%.

Target's margin lead over Walmart holds so far, but most of it came from tariff refunds. In the quarter that ended August 1, 2026, tariff refunds added 3.7 percentage points to Target's 9.6% operating margin, management said on the August 19 call. Without them, the operating margin would have been 5.9%, against 5.2% a year earlier. Excluding the refunds, management said the gross margin rose about 1 percentage point from a year earlier as Target lapped heavy markdowns and grew its higher-margin revenue streams.

Which Parts Of Target's Business Are Growing?

Target's sales are growing again, but two large categories are lagging. Sales rose 5.3% from a year earlier in the quarter that ended August 1. This marked the second rise in a row following a fall in the quarter that ended January 31.

Management said comparable sales rose 3.8%, driven by more shoppers. It said traffic rose 3.6%, and the average purchase was about flat. Online sales grew faster than store sales, led by more than 25% growth in same-day delivery.

title: Walmart's Combined Membership Likely Strengthens 'Value Proposition,' Oppenheimer Says
detail:
PREMIUM
Walmart's Combined Membership Likely Strengthens 'Value Proposition,' Oppenheimer Says
MT Newswires
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:05 AM MST 1 min read
WMT
AMZN
COST
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart's (WMT) new $120 membership combining Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus strengthens the retailer's "value proposition" and could drive incremental market share gains, particularly in delivery and e-commerce, Oppenheimer said in a report Thursday.

The firm said consumers are the "clear winners," as the combined membership offers $98 in savings compared with buying the two memberships separately and includes home delivery from both Walmart and Sam's Club without markups.

The offering further strengthens Walmart's membership proposition versus Amazon's (AMZN) Prime and Costco Wholesale (COST) and could support additional "wallet share gains" if adoption is strong. However, the firm expects a near-term "P&L headwind" and said the longer-term financial impact is "less clear," according to the report.

Oppenheimer has a perform rating on Walmart and continues to see a "balanced risk/reward" for its shares, citing long-term benefits from market-share gains, e-commerce and AI investments, while noting near-term risks from potentially softer comparable sales and an elevated valuation, the report said.

Walmart (NasdaqGS:WMT) introduced a new US$120 annual bundle that combines Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus memberships in a single offer.

The combined plan is pitched at value focused households that regularly use both Walmart's online services and Sam's Club warehouse clubs.

The US Food and Drug Administration issued Walmart a warning letter over unapproved sexually transmitted infection drug products sold on its marketplace.

The STI products were offered through Walmart's online third party platform, which uses Walmart Fulfillment Services for logistics and delivery.

The new Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus bundle and the FDA's warning on STI drug listings both feed into broader themes our research has highlighted. Check out 2 other big wins that Walmart investors should know about.

Walmart runs a vast network of retail and wholesale outlets alongside ecommerce sites and mobile apps worldwide, so a joint membership that links Walmart+ with Sam's Club Plus directly targets households already moving between its stores, warehouses and online marketplace, while regulators pay closer attention to how that ecosystem is run.

Does the team leading Walmart have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

What Walmart's bundle and FDA warning really signal for the Narrative

For Walmart, the joint Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus offer fits directly into the existing Narrative catalyst around higher margin profit pools such as memberships and other fee based services. A single US$120 plan encourages heavier use of both ecosystems and can deepen loyalty, which aligns with analysts focusing on membership income as a contributor to earnings quality. The FDA warning highlights one of the flagged risks instead, where compliance and scrutiny around digital tools and marketplace operations could add cost and operational friction, particularly as Walmart Fulfillment Services expands.

The biggest opportunity for eBay may be a business the company bought just this summer. This matters to shareholders right now, because eBay (EBAY) stock returned 30.1% over the past year against 16.5% for the S&P 500. The company closed the cash purchase on July 30, 2026, and management expects the business to start adding to its adjusted operating profit in 2028. What did eBay buy, and is there any sign it is working?

eBay Bought Depop, Whose Buyer Count Is Rising

eBay bought Depop, a brand with a strong reach among younger consumers, to go after what management calls a huge underpenetrated opportunity in U.S. consumer-to-consumer fashion. The early sign is Depop's own growth. On the August call, management said Depop had about 7 million buyers when eBay announced the deal, and close to 9 million by the end of June. Because this growth arrived before the deal closed, it is Depop's own doing, not yet eBay's doing.

eBay's own consumer selling points the same way. During the June quarter, the company's consumer-to-consumer GMV, the value of goods sold between individuals on eBay, grew by over 20%, outpacing total GMV growth of 14%. Depop therefore adds to the part of eBay that was already growing faster than the marketplace as a whole.

When eBay is a large share of what you own, your plan waits on the same catalyst. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Much Can Depop Add To eBay's Growth?

Management expects Depop to add roughly 1 percentage point to eBay's revenue growth in 2026, representing a small step. eBay paid $1.4 billion in cash for Depop, or about 2.6% of the company's market value of $54.7 billion.

The room to grow lies in the U.S., where management's analysis puts the online share of second-hand fashion sold between consumers in the low single digits, well below Europe.

eBay stock closed at $122.90 on October 21, 2026, landing within a cent of its highest close over the past year. The stock trades at 24.6 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 23.0 for the S&P 500. With Depop adding so little in 2026, that price appears to assume the core eBay marketplace keeps growing.

What Does Depop Have To Prove For eBay?

Depop has to grow without costing eBay profit growth for long. Management guides adjusted operating income growth of 10% to 12% for 2026, including Depop. The company expects Depop to hold that growth back by about 2 percentage points.

Rivals present the other worry. During the August call, an analyst noted that consumer-to-consumer selling is accelerating and that several competitors are investing heavily in it. Management said its Depop spending goes mainly to marketing and to cheaper shipping, adding that part of this investment is paid for with money eBay already spends marketing its own consumer selling and fashion.

Costco Wholesale (COST) stock returned 7.3% over the past year, compared with 16.5% for the S&P 500. Investors hoping for more run into a basic math problem. Costco generated $303 billion of revenue over its latest fiscal year, so a new business must be very large before it registers in the overall totals. Yet one part of Costco is growing about twice as fast as the company. So which part is it, and how far has it come?

Costco's Digital Sales Are Growing Twice As Fast

That fast-growing segment is digital. Costco's digitally enabled sales, a measure that includes orders handled by third-party delivery services, exceeded $33 billion in fiscal 2026. The category grew more than 20%, compared with 10.1% for Costco's total revenue over the same year.

The latest quarter displayed the same performance gap. During fiscal Q4 2026, Costco's digitally enabled comparable sales rose 19.5%, compared with 9.4% for all of its comparable sales.

Costco's newest digital push is only weeks old, meaning its impact is still ahead. In the weeks before its September 24, 2026 earnings call, Costco announced that its Uber Eats partnership is expanding from 17 states to the entire U.S. Management also said its DoorDash partnership now covers the U.S. as well. Separately, management said website traffic originating from AI search grew by triple digits for a second consecutive quarter, adding that those visits convert into orders at a higher rate than any other traffic to the site.

When Costco Wholesale is a large share of what you own, your plan waits on the same catalyst. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Big Is Digital Next To All Of Costco?

Digitally enabled sales accounted for about 11% of Costco's revenue in fiscal 2026. That makes digital a large business operating inside a much larger one. At Costco's current scale, the online segment adds to growth rather than changing what the company is.

The share price appears to assume Costco keeps growing faster than the market. Costco stock trades at 48.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 23.0 for the S&P 500. The shares closed on October 21, 2026, sitting 8.6% below their highest close of the past year, reached on May 19, 2026. The 48.0 multiple is already measured at that lower price, and faster digital growth is one way Costco could live up to it.

What Does Costco's Online Push Still Have To Prove?

Costco still has to show that delivery brings in members who spend more over time. During the fiscal Q4 2026 call, management was asked whether third-party delivery serves as Costco's long-term answer for delivery. Management called the option a great addition and said the people who use it most tend to be younger customers.
